mode: read-only -- no rehearsal, no publication, no corpus mutation of any kind performed to produce this audit

methodology.tool: custom corpus-wide link-existence checker (not migration/links.py scan, which is scoped to a move manifest and blind to this exact bug class -- confirmed by Agent 44's own commit message)
methodology.method: Fetched full content for all 513 active pages fresh via GET /api/v1/pages/<rid> (two passes: pre-repair at 2026-07-30T13:5x, post-repair at 2026-07-30T14:04). Extracted every inline markdown link [text](target), stripped anchors, resolved relative targets against the source page's own directory, and checked existence against the live path set. External/mailto/anchor-only links excluded. Reference-style link definitions ([text][id] / [id]: url) checked separately -- none found in the pages under dispute.
known_scope_limits: Anchor-level validity is not checked, only page-level existence (2 of the original 20 baseline protected_refs use anchors and are outside this checker's scope, consistent with them not appearing in either audit pass).

Does not verify whether a broken target actually serves an HTTP 200 via a redirect (i.e. does not distinguish 'no page at this literal path' from 'no page at this path AND no working redirect') -- a target is 'broken' here in the page-existence sense used throughout this programme's own baseline documentation, not in the HTTP sense.

pre_existing_unchanged_baseline.method: Matched by exact (source_path, line, raw_target) triple against the original pass-final-audit.json protected_refs list (20 entries) + the 1 unresolved Pi4 #78 entry, captured before any of this session's moves. 18 of these 21 known entries reproduce byte-for-byte; the other 2 use anchors outside this checker's page-existence scope (operations/platform/ceph-operations.md, operations/runbooks/deployment-checklist.md) and simply don't register as broken by this method -- not evidence they are fine or broken, just outside scope.

final_confirmation_after_agent44_second_.methodology_difference_noted: Commit 17fc368 tests whether a raw link ever resolved to a live page (tracked by resolved-target), which can classify a link as not-a-new-regression if its OLD resolved target was already non-existent (evidence-surface/baseline). This audit tests whether the specific (source, line, raw_target) occurrence currently resolves, matched against the exact same original 20-entry protected_refs baseline. Both are legitimate tests but disagree on these 2 entries because the resolved TARGET changed even though the source page classification (already-broken-before) did not -- a reader following either link today reaches a nonexistent page regardless of the internal classification.
